findings.statement: Within the searches stated below, no UK law or other binding instrument placing duties on developers of frontier or general-purpose AI models was located; this is not a finding that no such instrument exists. The 2024 King's Speech said the government would seek such legislation; the 2026 briefing notes contain none of the searched terms; the memoranda with developers state that they are not legally binding; and title searches of legislation.gov.uk for 2023–2026 found one instrument with "artificial intelligence" in its title, which places a duty on the Information Commissioner, not on developers.

passages.locator: Speech text, after the Employment Rights Bill item
passages.quote: It will seek to establish the appropriate legislation to place requirements on those working to develop the most powerful artificial intelligence models.
This memorandum is voluntary, not legally binding, and without prejudice to any binding agreements.
The Commissioner must prepare an appropriate code of practice giving guidance as to good practice in the processing of personal data

search.read: King's Speech 2026 background briefing notes (whole PDF, 39,000 words); legislation.gov.uk Atom feeds for all legislation with "artificial intelligence" in the title, years 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026, and with "frontier" in the title, same years; the one instrument found (SI 2026/425), whole text as made.

setAside.locator: King's Speech 2026 notes, PDF p. 126 (Cyber Security and Resilience Bill item)
setAside.reason: Mentions AI models' cyber capabilities and the AI Security Institute; places no duty on AI developers in the passage read. The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is a bill, not law, and its text was not inspected.
Requires the Information Commissioner to prepare a code of practice on personal-data processing in developing and using AI; the duty falls on the Commissioner, and the code is guidance.

findings.limits: Title searches do not find AI provisions inside Acts with other titles; the full text of UK legislation was not searched. Bills before Parliament are not legislation and were not searched. The method was checked by a control search ("online safety", 2023, returns the Online Safety Act 2023). The cross-family check confirmed the three quoted passages but did not reproduce the title searches or read the 2026 briefing notes.

findings.statement: Apart from the two rows, no binding duty on developers was found in the federal texts on the frameworks-and-law page, as read for this pack: Executive Order 14409 of 2 June 2026 provides for a voluntary access framework and states that it authorises no licensing requirement; the others are executive orders directing agencies, voluntary commitments, guidance, a policy plan or proposals. The no-licensing clause concerns the voluntary framework in section 3; it does not displace other law. The cross-family check confirmed the section 3(c) passage only, not the reading of the other texts.
